assessments.assessment: One shared frame and two solid arrowed axes retained. O is the common origin; sigma and epsilon are named as stress and strain. No numeric ticks, units, lattice or additional frame invent a quantitative scale.

O-A-B-C-D-E-K order retained. Straight proportional OA, nonlinear AB/BC, horizontal CD, rising DE and falling terminal EK are clear. B is below C/D; E is the maximum; K is right/below E. The SVG path endpoints coincide with all seven defining points. Drawing coordinates/interpolation are nonquantitative schematic layout, not data.

Exactly three solid horizontal guides terminate at A, B and E respectively; B's elastic guide is not incorrectly moved to CD. The English Prop./Elastic/Ultimate role labels correspond to the source historical stress labels and approved text; none is an invented tick value.

Exactly three solid vertical projections: A to Q, E to an unlabeled foot and K to P, all on the strain axis. Q remains left of E's foot and P remains right of it. No extra projection, dashed unloading trajectory or new label at E's foot is introduced.

All curve segments, axes and six guides are solid in source and SVG. Local labels O/A/B/C/D/E/K/Q/P are complete and unambiguous. Schematic is separately understood as a modern caution, not an original label. No answer-bearing annotation or cultural/Cyrillic/Chinese text leaks into the visible figure.

The full bilingual prose, not the SVG alone, defines engineering stress as force/original area and engineering strain as extension/original gauge length. CD is solid plastic yielding for particular materials. E is maximum engineering tensile stress; K is subsequent fracture. A post-E drop does not require falling local true stress. Residual 0.1%, the one-percent difference and the range 1.7 to 10 remain attributed conventions/illustrations. n=ultimate/allowable is not a universal structural-safety guarantee; actual stress, deformation, stability, fatigue, connections and other failure conditions remain qualified.
